records.rationale: All five paths read. Retain schedule-entry skip hook and fork/exit notifications as generic Android vendor source interfaces. Title/message claim bounded CFS hint deferral, but actual core adds only callbacks: no timer, cap, task-class check or SM_PREEMPT-only gate. __schedule invokes it for voluntary blocking too, after schedule_debug and before hrtick clear/IRQ disable/rq lock. A callback must implement all eligibility/bounds and must not bypass required blocking. Fork notification is at successful copy_process tail; exit follows seccomp release before accounting. No framework hint implementation was established in scoped SDK sources. Default false preserves all subsequent native scheduling; do not advertise an implemented bounded policy.

security: These hooks are powerful trusted-kernel policy overrides. Suppression can defeat immediate rescheduling, idle wakeup or required blocking, and can cause starvation, spinning or hangs if callbacks are wrong. No scheduler-enforced timeout or deferral cap is implemented here. Without callbacks all suppression outputs are false/zero and native bodies continue. Retention serves requested Android vendor source compatibility; it is not endorsement of an unverified vendor policy or permission for unprivileged code to register callbacks.
uncertainty: Scoped local searches in GrapheneOS system/core, frameworks/base and manifest common-modules found no named hook consumer. The actual framework hint transport, callback bounds and SDK use are unresolved; no-consumer search is not omission proof. Generic interfaces retained conservatively; no future hardware support is added.
validation: Full patches, current sites, native-body comparisons and declaration/export checks. No new kernel source changes and no runtime/preemption/latency tests for this batch.
